How the RLB tests a scenario

Run the failure on a copy of the model

The matrix names the cause; the model shows how fast it develops.

Start

The design state: cycle running, every loop in AUTO.

Failure at t = 0

A controller output forced: MAN 0 % (shut) or 100 % (open).

Nobody acts

No operator; the SIS once off, once on.

Read

Time to the alarm, the trip point and the PSV set; the peak.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Every vessel, and each bed, has its own PSV.
  • Normal operation stays below 90 % of every set.
  • A blocked outlet with full flow sets each process load.
  • I-1 and I-4 act minutes before their PSVs.
  • V-100 and V-103 rely on the PSV after the controls.

Part 2 · Sizing the orifice

How large must each PSV orifice be?

Part 2 · the plan

Load, area, letter

  1. The governing loadK-100 at full speed, from the model's compressor curve
  2. API 520 gas sizingcritical flow through the nozzle, then the API 526 letter
  3. Firea gas-filled shell, and an adsorber that desorbs
  4. A pulsating sourceV-103 and the buffered check

Interactive · the compressor relation of the model

K-100 delivers almost its full flow against the set

A blocked outlet relieves whatever K-100 can push at the relieving pressure.

Model step(), 100 % speed$F=F_{max}\,(1.08-0.08\,P/5.2)(1-\Delta p_F/P_{atm})$

At the 7.60 bar a relieving pressure K-100 still pushes 26.6 mol/s: 2777 kg/h of air.

API 520 Part I · gas and vapour, SI units

What the sizing equation needs

$W$
relief load: mass flow the valve must pass
kg/h
$P_1,\ P_2$
relieving pressure; back pressure at the outlet
kPa a
$T,\ M,\ Z$
relieving temperature, molar mass, compressibility (1 here)
K, kg/kmol, –
$k$
heat-capacity ratio $c_p/c_v$; 1.40 for air, O2, N2
–
$K_d,\ K_b,\ K_c$
discharge 0.975; back-pressure and rupture-disc corrections, 1
–
$A$
required effective orifice area
mm²

Derivation step 1 of 2

Is the nozzle flow critical?

Gas through a nozzle chokes once the outlet is low enough.

$r_c=\left(\dfrac{2}{k+1}\right)^{k/(k-1)}$isentropic nozzle: sonic at the throat
$P_2/P_1\le r_c\ \Rightarrow\ \text{critical flow}$the outlet no longer affects the flow
$C=0.03948\sqrt{k\left(\dfrac{2}{k+1}\right)^{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}}$API 520 coefficient, SI units

$r_c$ critical pressure ratio; $C$ flow coefficient. At $k$ = 1.40: $r_c$ = 0.528, $C$ = 0.0270.

PSV-100 to atmosphere: $P_2/P_1$ = 1.013 / 7.60 = 0.133, critical.

Derivation step 2 of 2

Critical flow scales with $P_1$, not with $P_1-P_2$

$W=C\,K_d\,P_1\,K_b\,K_c\,A\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{T\,Z}}$choked mass flux grows with upstream pressure
$A=\dfrac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1\,K_b\,K_c}\sqrt{\dfrac{T\,Z}{M}}$solve for the area
$P_1=P_{set}+0.10\,(P_{set}-P_{atm})$10 % overpressure; minimum 0.207 bar; fire 21 %

Above $r_c$ (high back pressure) API 520 uses the subcritical form with $F_2$.

Worked calculation · PSV-100 step 1 of 2

The load case gives 460 mm²

The area equation$A=\dfrac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1}\sqrt{\dfrac{T\,Z}{M}}$
$P_1=7.0+0.10\times(7.0-1.013)=7.599\ \text{bar a}$set 7.0 bar a, 10 % overpressure
$W=26.63\times28.96\times3.6=2777\ \text{kg/h}$K-100 at 7.60 bar a, air, 45 °C
$A=\dfrac{2777}{0.0270\times0.975\times759.9}\sqrt{\dfrac{318.15}{28.96}}=460\ \text{mm}^2$$P_1$ in kPa a, $T$ in K

Interactive · API 520 + API 526

Which letter does a load need?

The area equation$A=\dfrac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1}\sqrt{\dfrac{T\,Z}{M}}$

Halve the set and the area about doubles: capacity per mm² follows the absolute relieving pressure.

$W=0.2772\,\sqrt{M\,P_1}\;A'\,\dfrac{(T_w-T_1)^{1.25}}{T_1^{1.1506}}$

m²
$T_w$

K
$T_1$

K

Interactive · vessel and elevation

How much of the shell can a pool fire reach?

Raising a vessel shrinks its fire load; above 7.6 m no fire case remains.

API 521 · what the fire case really asks

The valve does not save a gas-filled shell

Gas does not cool the wall

Steel nears 600 °C and fails below the set.

Depressure instead

V-100 by PV-103; V-102 by FV-125 and XV-127.

Adsorbers desorb

Hot zeolite releases N2: +1587 kg/h. PSV-110: H → J.

Is fire credible?

Oil-free unit: without fire, three orifices shrink.

Interactive · V-103 with PV-133 shut, one cycle of the model's inflow

A 50 m³ buffer absorbs the blowdown pulses

Holding $P_1$ through the pulses would take a Q; the 50 m³ volume lets N keep V-103 below its accumulation limit.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • The load is K-100's full flow at the relieving pressure.
  • Critical flow: area ∝ W / P₁; low sets need large valves.
  • Fire sets every letter: an upper bound here.
  • A pulsating source is checked against the accumulation limit.

Part 3 · Around the valve

What must the piping, the discharge and the vessel do around the valve?

Part 3 · the plan

Upstream, downstream, and emptying the vessel

  1. Inlet loss and back pressurethe 3 % and 10 % rules at rated flow
  2. Where the gas goesoxygen and N2-rich plumes, and noise
  3. Depressuringemptying a vessel through its own valves
  4. What the document hands onnine engineering queries

API 520 Part II and Part I · conventional valve

The valve must see its own set, not the piping

An orifice is chosen; now the pipes on both sides must let it work.

$\Delta P_{in}\le 3\,\%\ \text{of}\ (P_{set}-P_{atm})$larger inlet loss: the valve chatters
$P_{b}-P_{atm}\le 10\,\%\ \text{of}\ (P_{set}-P_{atm})$built-up back pressure cuts the lift
$W=W_{rated}$ of the chosen orificethe valve passes its capacity, not the load

Line lengths 1 m inlet, 3–10 m tail and fittings are assumed.

Interactive · pick a PSV and the two line sizes

The valve's own flange sizes are too small

Two piping rules$\Delta P_{in}\le3\,\%\qquad P_b-P_{atm}\le10\,\%$

One line size up on each side passes both rules: DN65 inlet, DN100 tail on the three J valves.

Interactive · free-jet dilution, screening

How far until the air is breathable again?

$x=k_c\,d\,\sqrt{\rho_j/\rho_a}\;\Delta c_0/\Delta c$

$d$ outlet bore; $\rho_j/\rho_a$ gas / air density; $\Delta c$ O2 excess over air.

For the same outlet, oxygen needs about five times the distance: 23.5 % lies closer to air than 19.5 %.

Interactive · API 521 noise screening

A lifting PSV is loud even at 30 m

$L_{30}=L+10\log_{10}\!\left(\tfrac12 W c^2\right)$

$L$ from the pressure ratio (assumed); $W$ in kg/s; $c$ sonic speed, m/s.

The blow-off acts at every hold: frequent and loud, so it carries a silencer.

Emptying a vessel through its own valve

The model's valve relation empties the vessel

In a fire the protection is depressuring, so how fast can each vessel be emptied?

$\dfrac{dn}{dt}=-g_v(C,P,P_{atm})$the model's gv(): IEC gas valve, $x\le0.5$
$P=\dfrac{nRT_0}{V}\quad\text{or}\quad P=P_0\left(\dfrac{n}{n_0}\right)^{k}$isothermal, or adiabatic remaining gas
$P(t_{15})\le P_{atm}+0.5\,(P_{des}-P_{atm})$API 521: half the design gauge in 15 min

$n$ gas held, mol; $C$ model valve constant; $V$ volume; $T_0$ start temperature; $k$ = 1.4.

Interactive · from the PSV set, the vent fully open

Which vessel empties in time?

V-102's small product valve needs 7 min to half its design gauge: inside 15 min, the slowest of the three.

Engineering queries for the Project & deliverables tab

The document hands on nine open questions

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Inlet ≤ 3 %, back pressure ≤ 10 % at the rated flow: one size up.
  • Oxygen outlets need a zone about 15 m long.
  • Fire protection is depressuring: V-102 halves in 7 min.
  • Nine queries go to the project, among them the model's relief coefficient.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Start from the pressure ladder: operation ≤ 90 % of the set.

2

Size for the full flow behind a blocked outlet, from the model.

3

Use the relieving pressure in kPa absolute: low sets need large orifices.

4

Check inlet and tail at the rated flow, not at the load.

5

Protect gas-filled vessels in a fire by depressuring.
